- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast gently to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 days, apply downward bias adjustment proportional to sentiment magnitude.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast smoothness to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.  
- If true outcome deviates > 1.5σ from 18-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean unless sentiment strongly contradicts.
